rules.rule: These files define Kubernetes CRD and aggregated-API types for the GPUStack Operator. Flag: any breaking change to existing fields (renames, removals, type or json-tag changes) — the API must stay backward compatible; desired spec and observed status mixed together — they are strictly separated; kubebuilder validation markers weakened or removed without justification. A types change must be accompanied by regenerated output (`make generate`); that output is excluded from this review, so state the requirement as a reminder — never claim the regenerated files are present or absent.

Admission webhook sources. Flag: webhook and API inputs used without validation — external data (labels, CR fields, node metadata) is untrusted; admission behavior that drifts from the gates documented in docs/modules/devices/admission.md. A webhook change must be accompanied by the regenerated output (`make generate` produces the zz_generated.webhooks.go files); that output is excluded from this review, so state the requirement as a reminder — never claim it is present or absent. A bug fix here must ship a regression test in the same PR; `**/*_test.go` is excluded from this review, so state that the same way — as a reminder, never as a claim that a test is present or absent.

GPUStack Operator controller code. Flag violations of these invariants: reconcile logic is idempotent, level-based (no edge-triggered assumptions), and safe to retry; context.Context is propagated through call paths; errors are handled explicitly — never panics for control flow. The Devices CR ledger is the single authoritative allocation record: every allocation path must have a matching release path, and nothing reads or writes allocation state outside the ledger. Pool isolation: one ClusterQueue per pool, no cross-pool borrowing. Accelerator quota is integer credits (one accelerator = 1,600,000 credit units) — flag floating-point or percentage arithmetic. Layer ownership: label algebra belongs in pkg/nodefeature, device detection/allocation in pkg/devicemanager, Kueue scheduling-chain materialization in pkg/worker controllers, admission rules in the webhooks / AdmissionCheck controllers — flag feature logic leaking into shared or general-purpose packages. A bug fix here must ship a regression test in the same PR; `**/*_test.go` is excluded from this review, so state that as a reminder — never claim a test is present or absent, and never infer its absence from not having seen it. At the CGO boundary (callers of binding/ and of the csrc/ preload shims): C-returned memory ownership and vendor-library error codes are handled correctly, and injected preload paths and values stay quoted and escaped. Performance: no unbounded lists or per-object API round-trips in reconcile hot paths; watches scoped to resources that actually affect desired state.

Hand-written C preload shims that interpose on vendor accelerator libraries inside sliced workload containers. Flag: symbol-interposition hazards (dlsym/RTLD_NEXT misuse, assumptions about versioned symbols), unchecked error returns from vendor libraries, allocations without a matching free path, and unsynchronized shared state across threads.

GPUStack Operator Helm chart. Flag: template changes that alter a documented knob or default without a corresponding values.yaml entry. Two invariants of this chart are enforced in CI (chart.yml) and involve files excluded from this review, so state them as reminders rather than verifying: values.yaml changes must ship regenerated README.md and values.schema.json (`make generate chart`), and the vendored subchart trees under chart/charts/* change only via patch files under hack/ (`make deps`).

This repository's documentation follows a strict contract; `make lint docs` enforces the mechanical half, so focus on what lint cannot check. Use docs/README.md#module-map to locate guides, owning specs, code entry points and related modules before making a behavioral claim. Confirm the reviewed checkout and dependency versions; distinguish source statements from inference. Every page except the docs/README.md index keeps a short introduction, a `## Contents` list mirroring its `##` headings, and a footer with `**See also**` (required) and `**Next**` (expected wherever a next step exists); a new page must be registered in the All-pages table of docs/README.md with a label matching the page's H1 exactly. A fact is stated once — every other page links to it; flag duplicated facts. The module map owns shared routing and skill associations; update it when those associations change. llms.txt and Markdown site exports are generated from existing sources, not separately maintained. docs/getting-started/architecture.md is the overview and is capped near 200 lines: new mechanisms, rationale, or tables belong on a deep page under docs/modules/, and the overview gains at most one clause and a link. Decision rationale belongs in specs/, not in docs/ — docs state the rule that resulted. Tables pinned to code must change together with it: docs/reference/instance-type-unit-resources.md with pkg/nodefeature/unit_resources_preset.yaml, and docs/reference/settings.md with the GPUSTACK_* variable readers in pkg/worker/settings.

The repository front page. The accelerator matrix is a Yes/dash capability summary: verify resource names and manufacturer partition kinds against pkg/nodefeature/knowns.go, and logical slicing against each detector's LogicalSliced support. Per-card slice counts and isolation mechanisms belong in docs/modules/devices/discovery.md. Shared ownership limits belong in docs/modules/devices/requests.md and must match SharedResourceMaxSize; do not require them in the README matrix. Usage request shapes stay in sync with docs/modules/devices/requests.md — change both together. Link facts already owned by a guide instead of repeating them, and avoid prose counts of extensible lists.
